prompt:
Image 1 is a sprite sheet from the video game Factorio: 16 animation frames of a "biter" creature running, laid out in a 4x4 grid read left to right, top to bottom. Every frame faces the same direction (towards the bottom-right of the image) and is seen from the game's fixed high three-quarter top-down camera.

Redraw this sprite sheet with the creature replaced by a realistic boxelder bug (Boisea trivittata). Images 2 and 3 are photographs of the species, for anatomy and colouring only: a flat, elongated body; charcoal-black forewings with thin bright red-orange edges and veins; three red-orange stripes on the pronotum; small red eyes; six thin black legs; two long, thin, segmented black antennae.

For every frame keep exactly: the grid layout, the frame's position and size within its cell, the heading direction, the camera angle, and the leg positions, so the frames still play as a smooth looping run cycle. The bug should cover about the same area as the biter's body and legs.

Style: Factorio's pre-rendered 3D sprite art: realistic, slightly desaturated, lit softly from the top-left, with detail that stays readable when shrunk. Fully transparent background. No shadow on the ground, no grid lines, no text, no labels, no extra creatures.
note: first prototype, adopted as the anchor source; its prompt predates the template in gen-art.py
